# Star-delta starter -- OpenPLC starter

*Generated by `tools/gen_starters.py` from the scene's tag set. Do not edit by
hand; regenerate. The program's logic section is yours.*

**The task.** Start the motor in star -- main and star contactors -- change over to delta when motor.speed reaches the speed on the panel's pot, and drop everything on Stop. The changeover timing is yours: there is no timer in the starter. Star and delta closed together is a short circuit, and contacts close in 30 ms but take 45 ms to stop conducting, so wait for motor.staraux to fall before you energise delta.

**Done when.** The motor runs up in star, changes over at the pot's speed with a modest current step, and runs on in delta, and motor.breaker never drops. Drop star and energise delta in the same scan and the breaker trips, and stays tripped until somebody closes it by hand at the starter. Then load the machine (the starter's Motor Load) and start again: the star run-up takes about twice as long, so a changeover timed in seconds comes half way up it and draws nearly the direct-on-line current. Only motor.speed knows when the motor is ready.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`star_delta_start.st`](star_delta_start.st) | Every I/O point declared at its located address, with an empty logic section. |
| [`mbconfig.cfg`](mbconfig.cfg) | The Slave Device entry that points OpenPLC's Modbus master at the sidecar. |

The walkthrough for OpenPLC itself -- installing, compiling, timing,
troubleshooting -- is [`docs/OPENPLC.md`](../../../docs/OPENPLC.md). This page
is only what is different about this scene.

## Run it

1. Open the scene in FactoryForge: pick "Star-delta starter" on the start screen (or launch with --scene=res://templates/star_delta_start.json).
2. **Then** start the sidecar as the Modbus slave. The order matters: the
   addresses below are the ones it hands out for this scene's tags, and a
   sidecar that was already running when you changed scene keeps its old
   addresses and puts the new tags above them.

   ```bash
   factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver modbus-tcp -o port 5502
   ```

   (From a source checkout: `cd sidecar && python -m factoryforge_sidecar connect ...`.
   If OpenPLC runs in WSL or a VM, add `-o host 0.0.0.0` and read the warning
   it prints.) Check the address map it prints against the table below.
3. Compile `star_delta_start.st` in OpenPLC (web UI *Programs -> Upload*, or copy it
   into `webserver/st_files/` and run `./scripts/compile_program.sh star_delta_start.st`)
   and copy `mbconfig.cfg` to `webserver/core/`,
   or enter these numbers in *Slave Devices -> Add new device*
   (Generic Modbus TCP device, port 5502, slave id 1):

| Block | Start | Size |
|---|---|---|
| Discrete Inputs (%IX100.0) | 0 | 9 |
| Coils (%QX100.0) | 0 | 8 |
| Input Registers (%IW100) | 0 | 6 |
| Holding Registers - Read (%IW100) | 0 | 0 |
| Holding Registers - Write (%QW100) | 0 | 2 |

4. Start the PLC. To have it marked instead, run the grader in place of the
   3D scene -- same tags, same addresses -- and pass the port it prints:

   ```bash
   python tools/grade.py --scene star-delta-start
   factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver modbus-tcp --port <bus port it printed> -o port 5502
   ```

## I/O

`PLC writes` is an output (a motor, a valve, a lamp); `PLC reads` is an input
(a sensor, a button, a measurement). *Brief* marks the signals the task names;
the rest are there to be used, such as each drive's fault contact. Modbus
addresses are decimal, as the sidecar prints them: `0x10` is coil ten.

| Tag | Direction | Type | Modbus | In the program | Meaning | Brief |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `current_gauge.value` | PLC writes | float | 4x0 + 4x1 | `CurrentGaugeValueHi` %QW100 + `CurrentGaugeValueLo` %QW101 -> `CurrentGaugeValue` : REAL | needle position, scale 0..120 A | yes |
| `motor.breaker` | PLC reads | bit | 1x0 | `MotorBreaker` %IX100.0 | motor breaker, normally closed: TRUE = closed; trips on a star-delta short and stays tripped | yes |
| `motor.current` | PLC reads | float | 3x0 + 3x1 | `MotorCurrentHi` %IW100 + `MotorCurrentLo` %IW101 -> `MotorCurrent` : REAL | line current, A (full load 20 A) | yes |
| `motor.delta` | PLC writes | bit | 0x0 | `MotorDelta` %QX100.0 | delta contactor coil -- NEVER with star: together they short the supply | yes |
| `motor.deltaaux` | PLC reads | bit | 1x1 | `MotorDeltaaux` %IX100.1 | delta contacts conducting | yes |
| `motor.main` | PLC writes | bit | 0x1 | `MotorMain` %QX100.1 | main contactor coil: feeds the motor windings | yes |
| `motor.mainaux` | PLC reads | bit | 1x2 | `MotorMainaux` %IX100.2 | main contacts conducting | yes |
| `motor.overload` | PLC reads | bit | 1x3 | `MotorOverload` %IX100.3 | thermal overload, normally closed: TRUE = OK, FALSE = tripped | yes |
| `motor.speed` | PLC reads | float | 3x2 + 3x3 | `MotorSpeedHi` %IW102 + `MotorSpeedLo` %IW103 -> `MotorSpeed` : REAL | motor speed, % of synchronous | yes |
| `motor.star` | PLC writes | bit | 0x2 | `MotorStar` %QX100.2 | star contactor coil: ties the winding ends together (a third of the torque) | yes |
| `motor.staraux` | PLC reads | bit | 1x4 | `MotorStaraux` %IX100.4 | star contacts conducting -- still TRUE for 45 ms after its coil drops | yes |
| `panel.estop` | PLC reads | bit | 1x5 | `PanelEstop` %IX100.5 | E-stop, normally closed: TRUE = healthy, FALSE = pressed; stays pressed until pulled out | yes |
| `panel.green` | PLC writes | bit | 0x3 | `PanelGreen` %QX100.3 | green lamp on the panel |  |
| `panel.red` | PLC writes | bit | 0x4 | `PanelRed` %QX100.4 | red lamp on the panel |  |
| `panel.reset` | PLC reads | bit | 1x6 | `PanelReset` %IX100.6 | Reset button, momentary: a short pulse per press | yes |
| `panel.setpoint` | PLC reads | float | 3x4 + 3x5 | `PanelSetpointHi` %IW104 + `PanelSetpointLo` %IW105 -> `PanelSetpoint` : REAL | the operator's pot, 50..95 % (starts at 85) | yes |
| `panel.start` | PLC reads | bit | 1x7 | `PanelStart` %IX100.7 | Start button, momentary: a short pulse per press -- latch it | yes |
| `panel.stop` | PLC reads | bit | 1x8 | `PanelStop` %IX101.0 | Stop button, momentary: a short pulse per press | yes |
| `tower.green` | PLC writes | bit | 0x5 | `TowerGreen` %QX100.5 | tower lamp, green | yes |
| `tower.red` | PLC writes | bit | 0x6 | `TowerRed` %QX100.6 | tower lamp, red | yes |
| `tower.yellow` | PLC writes | bit | 0x7 | `TowerYellow` %QX100.7 | tower lamp, yellow | yes |

## Three things this scene's wiring does not forgive

- **A 32-bit value is two registers**, high word first. This scene has 4:
  `current_gauge.value`, `motor.current`, `motor.speed`, `panel.setpoint`. The
  program's first and last sections move them between the registers and plain
  DINT/REAL variables, so your logic never sees a register. OpenPLC's
  `DWORD_TO_REAL` converts the *number* (`16#3F800000` becomes 1065353216.0,
  not 1.0), so the starter rebuilds a REAL bit by bit instead.
  [`../check_starters.sh`](../check_starters.sh) compiles the helpers with
  OpenPLC's own matiec and checks them against two million bit patterns.
- **Anything polled can be missed if it is short.** OpenPLC's master reads
  every 50 ms. A button press in the 3D scene is one physics tick (about 17 ms)
  on the tag bus, so a click can fall between two polls; the grader holds each
  press for 0.15 s. The same goes the other way: hold an output you want the
  scene to see for well over one polling period.
- **An output you never write is FALSE.** The master rewrites the whole coil
  block on every poll, including coils your program does not touch.
